title: Squash Commits
definition: The process of combining multiple sequential commits into a single, cohesive commit to keep the repository history clean and meaningful.
simpleExplanation: Nobody wants to look at a history filled with 50 commits named 'wip', 'fixed typo', 'trying again', 'please work'. Squashing takes those 50 tiny, messy commits and crushes them together into a single, beautiful commit named 'Added Shopping Cart Feature'.
realWorldExample: GitHub has a massive green button called 'Squash and Merge' on Pull Requests. It automatically crushes your messy feature branch into one clean commit before merging it into `main`.
useCases: Maintaining a clean, readable git log

basic: What command is manually used to squash commits locally?
intermediate: Why do Open Source projects demand that you squash your commits before they accept your code?

answers.question: Why Open Source demands it?
answers.answer: Maintainers need to be able to easily read the project history. If a feature breaks 6 months later, they want to revert one single clean commit. They don't want to figure out which of your 40 'wip' commits caused the bug.
